basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 28/28 patients.
Congenital digit abnormalities and carpal, tarsal, metacarpal and metatarsal synostoses define the disorder.
Congenital myopathy with joint contractures; strabismus and hypermetropia in 1/1 assessed, with limited prevalence evidence. Restrictive ventilation reflects muscle weakness.
Defined by disease of the renal glomerulus; immune mechanisms are not universal across this umbrella.
B-lymphoblastic blood/marrow neoplasm within the leukemia/lymphoma spectrum; lymphoma warrants the immune mechanism axis.
Inherited metabolic disorder causes skeletal muscle destruction; renal insufficiency occurs in 30-79% through myoglobin toxicity. Transaminases can originate from muscle.
Cervical myelomeningocele involves spinal neural tissue and a congenital vertebral closure defect.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; eye abnormalities 30-79%, including optic/ocular defects; heart defects 30-79% (VSD 40%); urinary tract dysfunction includes vesicoureteral reflux in 30%.
Inflammation is located in tissues surrounding the kidney; the definition does not establish an infectious or autoimmune cause.
Progeroid skin/lipoatrophy, immunodeficiency and endocrine failure; cataract/progressive visual loss 80-99%. Neurologic, skeletal, dental, hepatic and cardiac findings omitted by cap.
Usher type 1 is defined by congenital hearing loss, vestibular dysfunction and progressive rod-cone retinal degeneration.
Site-unspecified mature teratomas are predominantly gonadal, usually ovarian. Extragonadal organ sites are minority subtypes; mature tissue contents do not identify an affected organ.
Thyroid hormone resistance; skeletal maturation defects and learning disability occur in 30-79%, with osteoporosis also described. Tachycardia alone does not establish cardiac damage.
Trigeminal nerve damage with sensory loss and persistent facial skin ulceration defines the syndrome.
AP4B1-related neurodevelopmental and corticospinal disease; structural skeletal findings are occasional or lack evidence of frequency above 30%.
Endocrine failure, neurodegeneration and alopecia define syndrome; hearing loss in 4/7 and annotated 80-99%. Frequent bone abnormalities omitted by cap; T-wave changes alone lack damage.
Acute infection of the fallopian tubes and ovaries, typically part of pelvic inflammatory disease; reproductive sites have no anatomical axis.
Intracranial arterial aneurysm is a vascular lesion; brain injury from rupture is not intrinsic to every aneurysm.
Localized amyloid mass of connective soft tissue; no evidence of systemic amyloid organ damage or an inborn metabolic disorder.
Adenocarcinoma arising in the lung; papillary architecture does not establish additional organ involvement.
Telomere biology disorders prominently include marrow failure. Skin, lung and liver damage cannot be assumed in >=30% across the combined short- and long-telomere spectrum.
Lysosomal glycoprotein degradation disorders; neurodevelopmental impairment and skeletal dysostosis each occur broadly across major subtypes (>30%). Organomegaly alone does not prove damage.
Bone fragility with recurrent fractures in 9/9; blue sclerae do not establish ocular dysfunction. Developmental delay reported in only 1/9.
Dysgenetic gonads cause hormone deficiency and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism; osteoporosis annotated 80-99%. Genital anomalies lack demonstrated urinary dysfunction; tumors are separate.
Congenital failure of fibular bone continuity and union creates a persistent false joint.
